note: First applied-questions batch: 4 comprehension passages (20 q), 15 synonyms, 15 antonyms, 10 sentence completion, 10 oral English; 41 Physics calculation/scenario questions (numerically verified).

passages.title: Mama Nkechi at Ogbete Market
passages.text: Every morning before dawn, Mama Nkechi arranges her tomatoes in neat pyramids at Ogbete Main Market in Enugu. She has sold vegetables there for twenty-two years, long enough to watch prices climb from a few kobo to hundreds of naira. Yet she does not complain about the cost of living the way younger traders do. 'The market teaches you patience,' she says, wiping her hands on her wrapper. 'Some days you sell everything; some days you carry your goods home. The trader who panics loses twice.' Her customers, many of whom she has known since they were children on their mothers' backs, rarely bargain hard with her. They know that her prices are fair and that she will slip an extra pepper into the bag of anyone who looks like they are struggling.

passages.title: A computer laboratory in Dala
passages.text: When Government Girls' Secondary School, Dala, received a solar-powered computer laboratory last year, many parents were sceptical. Computers, some argued, would distract the girls from their books. Twelve months later, the results have silenced most critics. The school recorded its best WAEC performance in a decade, and thirty students who had never touched a keyboard now type faster than their teachers. The principal attributes the change not to the machines themselves but to what they made possible: online past questions, video lessons in Hausa and English and, above all, a new confidence. 'The girls no longer see themselves as behind,' she explains. 'They see themselves as connected.' The challenge now is maintenance. Dust, heat and the occasional curious goat are constant threats, and the school's budget cannot stretch to a full-time technician.

passages.title: The floods in Lokoja
passages.text: The floods came to Lokoja in September, as they now do almost every year, but this time the town was ready. Months earlier, a group of secondary-school students had mapped the streets that always went under first and painted warning marks on walls to show how high the water had risen in previous years. When the Niger began to swell, volunteers moved elderly residents to higher ground before a single house was submerged. Not everyone was persuaded. Some traders refused to leave their shops, insisting that the river 'knew them' and would spare their goods. The river did not. Yet the overall picture was one of a community that had stopped waiting for help from Abuja and started helping itself. As one volunteer put it, 'We cannot stop the water, but we can stop the surprise.'

passages.title: Tunde's first day
passages.text: Tunde had rehearsed the sentence all the way from Abeokuta: 'Good morning, my name is Tunde Bakare and I am happy to be here.' But when the class teacher at his new school in Ibadan asked him to introduce himself, the words scattered like startled chickens. Forty pairs of eyes waited. A girl in the second row whispered something, and the whispers spread. Then a tall boy at the back stood up. 'Ma, he is the one who scored the highest in the entrance examination,' he announced, as though this settled the matter. The whispering stopped. Tunde never learnt why the boy, Chidi, had spoken for him, and Chidi never mentioned it again. But for the next six years, whenever Tunde faced a crowd, he remembered that the kindest thing a stranger can do is to give you a reason to be there.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: The main point of the passage is that Mama Nkechi
questions.A: sells the cheapest tomatoes in Enugu
questions.B: wants younger traders to leave the market
questions.D: has learnt patience and fairness from years of trading
questions.explanation: The passage centres on the patience she has learnt ('The market teaches you patience') and the fairness her customers rely on.

questions.B: bargaining is forbidden in Ogbete market
questions.D: they trust her to be fair
questions.explanation: The passage says they 'know that her prices are fair' — trust, not fear or rules, explains their behaviour.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The senator gave an EVASIVE answer when asked about the missing funds.
questions.explanation: Evasive means avoiding a direct answer — indirect.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The new bridge has ALLEVIATED the traffic problem in Apapa.
questions.explanation: To alleviate is to make a problem less severe — to reduce it.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: Her explanation of the accident was LUCID.
questions.explanation: Lucid means clearly expressed and easy to understand.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The chief was RELUCTANT to sign the agreement.
questions.explanation: Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The company has decided to CURTAIL its spending on advertising.
questions.explanation: To curtail is to reduce or cut short.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The lawyer's argument was so COGENT that the judge ruled in his favour.
questions.explanation: Cogent means clear, logical and convincing.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: Despite the heavy rain, the farmers remained OPTIMISTIC about the harvest.
questions.explanation: Optimistic means expecting a good outcome — hopeful.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The minister's remarks were widely regarded as PROVOCATIVE.
questions.explanation: Provocative remarks are intended to cause anger or strong reaction — inflammatory.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The village head is known for his BENEVOLENCE towards orphans.
questions.explanation: Benevolence is kindness and generosity.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The landlord issued an ULTIMATUM to the tenants.
questions.explanation: An ultimatum is a final demand or warning, with consequences if it is refused.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The students found the lecturer's explanation rather AMBIGUOUS.
questions.explanation: Ambiguous means open to more than one meaning — unclear.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The referee's decision was IMPARTIAL.
questions.explanation: Impartial means not favouring either side — fair.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The teacher COMMENDED the pupils for their neat handwriting.
questions.explanation: To commend is to praise formally.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The doctor advised him to ABSTAIN from alcohol.
questions.explanation: To abstain from something is to keep away from it completely.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: There has been a PROLIFERATION of private universities in Nigeria.
questions.explanation: Proliferation means rapid growth in number.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The witness gave a VAGUE description of the thief.
questions.explanation: Vague (unclear) is the opposite of precise.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The old man was FRUGAL with his money.
questions.explanation: Frugal means sparing with money; extravagant means spending freely and wastefully.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The road to the village is very NARROW.
questions.explanation: Narrow is the opposite of wide.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The manager's decision was HASTY.
questions.explanation: Hasty means made too quickly; the opposite is carefully thought through.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The two brothers are always in HARMONY.
questions.explanation: Harmony (agreement) is the opposite of conflict.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The chemical is extremely VOLATILE.
questions.explanation: Volatile means liable to change or evaporate rapidly; the opposite is stable.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: He is a very HUMBLE man.
questions.explanation: Humble (modest) is the opposite of arrogant.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The teacher's instructions were EXPLICIT.
questions.explanation: Explicit means stated clearly; the opposite is vague.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The government has decided to EXPAND the airport.
questions.explanation: Expand (make bigger) is the opposite of reduce.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The prices of foodstuffs have been FLUCTUATING since January.
questions.explanation: Fluctuating prices rise and fall; the opposite is stable.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The visitors were given a HOSTILE reception.
questions.explanation: Hostile (unfriendly) is the opposite of friendly.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The council's response to the complaint was PROMPT.
questions.explanation: Prompt means without delay; the opposite is delayed.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: She spoke in a very FORMAL manner.
questions.explanation: Formal is the opposite of casual or informal.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The team's performance this season has been MEDIOCRE.
questions.explanation: Mediocre means of only average quality; the opposite is excellent.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The soldiers made a COWARDLY retreat.
questions.explanation: Cowardly is the opposite of brave.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: Hardly had the referee blown the final whistle ____ the fans rushed onto the pitch.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly … when' is the fixed pair; 'no sooner … than' is the other.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: The principal, together with the teachers, ____ attending the conference in Abuja.
questions.explanation: A phrase beginning 'together with' does not change the number of the subject; 'the principal' is singular, so 'is'.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: If I ____ you, I would accept the scholarship.
questions.explanation: The unreal (hypothetical) condition takes 'were' for all persons: 'If I were you'.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: Neither the driver nor the passengers ____ injured in the accident.
questions.explanation: With 'neither … nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject — 'passengers', plural — so 'were'.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: She is one of the few students who ____ passed the examination.
questions.explanation: 'Who' refers to 'students' (plural), not to 'she', so the verb is plural: 'have passed'.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: The committee ____ its report to the governor last week.
questions.explanation: 'Last week' fixes the action in the simple past: 'submitted'.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: No sooner had we arrived at the station ____ the train left.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' is always followed by 'than'.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: He insisted ____ paying for the meal.
questions.explanation: 'Insist' takes the preposition 'on': insist on doing something.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: By this time next year, my sister ____ from the university.
questions.explanation: An action completed before a future point takes the future perfect: 'will have graduated'.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the gap: The more you practise past questions, ____ you become.
questions.explanation: The parallel comparative pattern is 'the more …, the more …'.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option to which the given sentence relates when the word in capitals is stressed: AMINA bought the red bag yesterday.
questions.A: Did Amina sell the red bag yesterday?
questions.B: Did Amina buy the blue bag yesterday?
questions.C: Did Aisha buy the red bag yesterday?
questions.D: Did Amina buy the red bag today?
questions.explanation: Stressing AMINA answers a question about WHO bought the bag — the option that names a different person.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option to which the given sentence relates when the word in capitals is stressed: The teacher punished the BOY for coming late.
questions.A: Did the teacher praise the boy for coming late?
questions.B: Did the teacher punish the girl for coming late?
questions.C: Did the principal punish the boy for coming late?
questions.D: Did the teacher punish the boy for fighting?
questions.explanation: Stress on BOY contrasts him with someone else who might have been punished — 'the girl'.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option to which the given sentence relates when the word in capitals is stressed: My uncle bought a NEW car in Lagos.
questions.A: Did your uncle buy a used car in Lagos?
questions.B: Did your aunt buy a new car in Lagos?
questions.C: Did your uncle buy a new car in Abuja?
questions.D: Did your uncle sell a new car in Lagos?
questions.explanation: Stress on NEW contrasts with the car's condition — 'used'.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option to which the given sentence relates when the word in capitals is stressed: Kemi will travel to Kano TOMORROW.
questions.A: Will Kemi travel to Kaduna tomorrow?
questions.B: Will Kemi fly to Kano tomorrow?
questions.C: Will Tope travel to Kano tomorrow?
questions.D: Will Kemi travel to Kano next week?
questions.explanation: Stress on TOMORROW contrasts the time of travel — 'next week'.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the option to which the given sentence relates when the word in capitals is stressed: The students SANG the anthem loudly.
questions.A: Did the teachers sing the anthem loudly?
questions.B: Did the students sing the anthem softly?
questions.C: Did the students recite the anthem loudly?
questions.D: Did the students sing the chorus loudly?
questions.explanation: Stress on SANG contrasts the action — 'recite'.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one represented by the letters in capitals: pLAY
questions.explanation: 'Play' has the /eɪ/ sound, as in 'weight'; 'said' is /e/, 'height' is /aɪ/, 'sit' is /ɪ/.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in capitals: CHurch
questions.explanation: 'Church' begins with /tʃ/, the sound in 'nature'; 'machine' and 'champagne' have /ʃ/, 'chemist' has /k/.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the one represented by the letters in capitals: bOOk
questions.explanation: 'Book' has the short /ʊ/ sound, as in 'pull'; 'food' and 'boot' have long /uː/, 'blood' has /ʌ/.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in capitals: THin
questions.explanation: 'Thin' has the voiceless /θ/, as in 'three'; 'this', 'those' and 'father' have the voiced /ð/.

questions.subject: Use of English
questions.q: Choose the word that rhymes with the word in capitals: BEAR
questions.explanation: 'Bear' is pronounced /beə/ and rhymes with 'pear'; 'fear', 'near' and 'dear' end in /ɪə/.

questions.explanation: Distance = area under the velocity–time graph: rectangle 10 × 4 = 40 m plus triangle ½ × 2 × 10 = 10 m; total 50 m.

questions.q: A net force of 20 N acts on a body of mass 5 kg. The acceleration produced is
questions.explanation: F = ma ⇒ a = F/m = 20/5 = 4 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 2 kg block on a rough horizontal table is pulled by a horizontal force of 10 N. If the frictional force is 4 N, the acceleration of the block is
questions.explanation: Net force = 10 − 4 = 6 N; a = F/m = 6/2 = 3 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An astronaut has a mass of 60 kg on Earth. On the Moon, where g = 1.6 m/s², her weight is
questions.explanation: Mass does not change; weight W = mg = 60 × 1.6 = 96 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A boy pushes a crate 4 m across a floor with a steady horizontal force of 50 N. The work done is
questions.explanation: Work = force × distance moved in the direction of the force = 50 × 4 = 200 J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A student of mass 60 kg climbs a flight of stairs 5 m high in 10 s. Taking g = 10 m/s², the average power developed is
questions.explanation: Power = work/time = mgh/t = (60 × 10 × 5)/10 = 300 W.

questions.explanation: Efficiency = (useful output/input) × 100 = (400/500) × 100 = 80%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 0.5 kg ball moving at 8 m/s strikes a wall and rebounds along the same line at 6 m/s. The magnitude of the change in momentum is
questions.explanation: Velocity reverses, so Δp = m(v + u) = 0.5 × (8 + 6) = 7 kg m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 2 kg trolley moving at 3 m/s collides with a stationary 1 kg trolley and the two move off together. Their common velocity is
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved: 2 × 3 + 1 × 0 = (2 + 1)v ⇒ v = 6/3 = 2 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A force of 50 N acts on a football for 0.2 s. The impulse given to the ball is
questions.explanation: Impulse = force × time = 50 × 0.2 = 10 N s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A lever is used to lift a load of 100 N with an effort of 20 N. If the velocity ratio of the lever is 8, its efficiency is
questions.explanation: MA = load/effort = 100/20 = 5; efficiency = (MA/VR) × 100 = (5/8) × 100 = 62.5%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block of mass 200 g has a volume of 250 cm³. When placed in water (density 1.0 g/cm³) it will
questions.A: sink because its density is 1.25 g/cm³
questions.B: float because its density is 0.8 g/cm³
questions.C: sink because it is heavier than 100 g
questions.D: float because its volume is greater than 200 cm³
questions.explanation: Density = mass/volume = 200/250 = 0.8 g/cm³, which is less than that of water, so it floats.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A box of mass 20 kg rests on a floor with its base area 0.5 m². Taking g = 10 m/s², the pressure it exerts on the floor is
questions.explanation: Pressure = force/area = (20 × 10)/0.5 = 400 Pa.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The pressure due to water at the bottom of a tank 3 m deep is (density of water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Pressure in a liquid = hρg = 3 × 1000 × 10 = 30 000 Pa.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A force of 5 N stretches a spring by 2 cm. Within the elastic limit, a force of 12.5 N will stretch it by
questions.explanation: Hooke's law: extension ∝ force. k = 5/2 = 2.5 N/cm, so e = 12.5/2.5 = 5 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The quantity of heat needed to raise the temperature of 2 kg of water from 20 °C to 70 °C is (specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/kg K)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The heat required to melt 0.5 kg of ice at 0 °C is (specific latent heat of fusion of ice = 336,000 J/kg)
questions.explanation: Q = mL = 0.5 × 336 000 = 168 000 J = 168 kJ. No temperature change occurs during melting.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A bimetallic strip made of brass and iron (brass expands more than iron) is heated. The strip will
questions.explanation: The brass side becomes longer than the iron side, so the strip curves with brass on the outside — it bends towards the iron.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A fixed mass of gas at 27 °C and 2 atm is heated at constant volume to 177 °C. The new pressure is
questions.explanation: Pressure law: P₁/T₁ = P₂/T₂ with temperatures in kelvin: 2/300 = P₂/450 ⇒ P₂ = 3 atm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 400 cm³ of a gas at 100 kPa is compressed to 200 kPa at constant temperature. The new volume is
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ ⇒ 100 × 400 = 200 × V₂ ⇒ V₂ = 200 cm³.

questions.explanation: The sound travels to the cliff and back: 2d = vt = 340 × 2 = 680 m ⇒ d = 340 m.

questions.q: A pipe closed at one end is 17 cm long. Taking the speed of sound as 340 m/s, the frequency of its fundamental note is
questions.explanation: For a closed pipe the fundamental has L = λ/4 ⇒ λ = 4 × 0.17 = 0.68 m; f = v/λ = 340/0.68 = 500 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object is placed 2 m in front of a plane mirror. If the object moves 0.5 m towards the mirror, the distance between the object and its image becomes
questions.explanation: The image is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front: new object distance 1.5 m, so object–image separation = 2 × 1.5 = 3.0 m.

questions.A: 6 cm from the lens, virtual and upright
questions.B: 30 cm from the lens, real and inverted
questions.C: 25 cm from the lens, real and upright

questions.explanation: Ohm's law: I = V/R = 12/4 = 3 A.
